claims.statement: The intelligence layer defines provider-neutral StructuredPrompt (with optional json_schema), SynthesisResult (with tool, explanation, and alternatives), SynthesisOptions (including local GGUF and structured_output knobs), and an exception hierarchy for unavailable, execution, and configuration failures.
`detect_synthesis_provider` returns only the configured provider when available and otherwise raises, so there is no automatic fallback chain between providers.
`synthesize` honors a backend override while preserving configured SynthesisConfig options, validates the provider, and lazy-loads and dispatches to local_gguf, ollama, openai_compatible, or tier0.
Prompt budgeting targets MAX_PROMPT_WORDS = 680, starting with up to 5 tools, 4 subcommands, 8 flags, and 4 examples per tool, and progressively reduces examples, flags, subcommands, then tools.

The system instruction restricts synthesis to retrieved ToolSpec context, forbids usage/synopsis echoes, requires a JSON object matching COMMAND_JSON_SCHEMA, and uses none=true when no listed tool fits.

`parse_synthesis_output` prefers structured JSON, strips language-tagged fences and shell prompts, rejects prose and usage echoes, records explicit none answers, and `SemService._repair_once` performs one repair retry when no command is extracted unless none was explicit.

The Ollama provider uses stdlib urllib.request (no ollama SDK or pip), resolves base_url or OLLAMA_HOST, passes format=COMMAND_JSON_SCHEMA and think to /api/chat (retrying without them if rejected), and calls /api/embed for embeddings.

The OpenAI-compatible provider resolves a base URL and bearer key from config, keyring, or environment, posts to /chat/completions with json_schema response_format (retrying without response_format on 400/422), and maps HTTP and connection failures separately.
FastEmbed caches one ONNX model per process in the application data directory, caps threads at four, and uses query_embed or passage_embed when the model supports them.

tier0 is always available offline and scores retrieved ToolSpec examples by query token overlap, returning a verified command when overlap is at least 0.55 and otherwise yielding cleanly to ToolSpec card fallback.

The local_gguf provider manages curated tiny, balanced, and quality Qwen2.5-Coder GGUF models and executes JSON-schema constrained synthesis via in-process llama-cpp-python or a managed ephemeral-port llama-server child process.

`verify_command` grounds the primary executable against PATH and builtins (skipping env assignments and wrapper flags), cross-checks expanded short/long flags against ToolSpec, and classifies commands as safe, caution, or destructive.
